::: {.tut-standfirst}
The home stretch: review the complete result, handle sensitive species and generate the Darwin Core Archive ready to publish on GBIF and SiBBr.
:::

## Preview

On the **Preview** tab, Saíra shows the final table already in Darwin Core vocabulary, with all corrections applied. This is the moment for one last general check:

- the columns have the correct Darwin Core names;
- required fields are filled in;
- names and coordinates were validated in the previous steps.

```{=html}

  <div class="frame"><span class="ph-label">screenshot · final preview</span></div>

</figure>
```

## Sensitive species

Before publishing, Saíra checks whether there are **threatened taxa** (based on the National List of Fauna/Flora — MMA). For those records, you can choose to **generalize the location** (reduce coordinate precision) or omit it, protecting vulnerable populations without giving up on publishing the data.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Sensitive data require a conscious decision
Generalizing coordinates of threatened species is a good practice recommended by GBIF and SiBBr. Assess case by case: the goal is to share knowledge without exposing the species to collection or persecution.
:::

## Generating the Darwin Core Archive

```{=html}
<ol class="steps">
  <li><strong>Review the metadata (EML).</strong>
    <p>Fill in the dataset title, institution, license and responsible parties — they go into the <span class="term">eml.xml</span>.</p></li>
  <li><strong>Generate the file.</strong>
    <p>Saíra assembles the <span class="term">.zip</span> package with <span class="term">occurrence.txt</span>, <span class="term">meta.xml</span> and <span class="term">eml.xml</span>.</p></li>
  <li><strong>Download and publish.</strong>
    <p>Download the Darwin Core Archive and send it to your IPT (GBIF/SiBBr) for publication.</p></li>
</ol>
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## What is a Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A)
It's a standardized `.zip` package: a data file (<span class="term">occurrence.txt</span>), a descriptor that states what each column means (<span class="term">meta.xml</span>) and the dataset metadata (<span class="term">eml.xml</span>). It's exactly what global repositories expect to receive.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Export failed or unavailable?
It's almost always an **empty required field** or a pending validation. Check that <span class="term">occurrenceID</span>, <span class="term">basisOfRecord</span>, <span class="term">scientificName</span> and <span class="term">eventDate</span> are filled in, and that the name and coordinate steps left no unresolved items. Saíra points out what's missing before releasing the download.
:::

## Publishing on GBIF and SiBBr

With the `.zip` in hand, publication happens outside Saíra, usually via your institution's or SiBBr's **IPT** (Integrated Publishing Toolkit). The file generated by Saíra is already in the expected format — just upload it and publish.

## Done

You took a raw spreadsheet all the way to a validated Darwin Core Archive. From here, your data can be discovered, cited and combined with collections worldwide. 🐦
